column1: # comment: "Tag alignments \u2014 SKOS, schema.org, Dublin Core, FOAF, W3C Web Annotation, MOAT and the Tag Ontology. The reified gmeow:Tagging relator (with provenance, confidence, temporal scope and suppression) is canonical; flat projections are lossy downcasts."

column6: MOAT distinguishes tag string from meaning URI; GMEOW's Tag IRI IS the meaning, with labels for synonyms

Wikidata 'tag' (metadata used for classification) — Wikidata's item leans toward the tag-as-string reading; GMEOW's Tag is an information-object individual whose IRI is the meaning and whose strings are labels, so closeMatch, not exactMatch; curl-validated 2026-07-03

A GMEOW Tag IS a skos:Concept — an information-object value identified by its IRI, surfaced by a label. The Tagging RELATOR (provenance/confidence/scope) is the close-but-distinct construct, not the Tag itself; so the Tag class reverses as an asserted fact, not a refutable claim.
A GMEOW TagScheme IS a skos:ConceptScheme — the namespace bucket for tags/concepts; class identity, parallels eqTags001.

Wikidata 'folksonomy' (classification based on users' tags) — a folksonomy is the emergent practice; a TagScheme is the namespace bucket the practice populates. Related, not equivalent: relatedMatch with the vagueness of the relationship stated rather than laundered into a low-confidence closeMatch; curl-validated 2026-07-03
GMEOW Tagging is a relator with provenance/confidence/temporal scope; oa:Annotation is a flatter annotation body — closeMatch, not exactMatch
Newman's Tag Ontology — GMEOW Tagging carries the same tripartite structure (tagger, resource, tag) with added provenance/confidence/temporal scope

Wikidata 'tagging' (the act of labelling data/content with a short string) — the same act, but GMEOW reifies it as a relator with tagger, scheme, confidence, interval, and suppression; closeMatch on the act, with the relator structure as GMEOW's surplus; curl-validated 2026-07-03
GMEOW broaderTag is transitive; skos:broader is the direct link (skos:broaderTransitive is transitive) — closeMatch, not exactMatch
lossy — schema:keywords is a text or URL value; GMEOW hasTag points to a structured Tag individual
Scheme membership IS skos:inScheme — a tag/concept belongs to a scheme; no transitivity caveat (unlike broaderTag), so this reverses as an asserted fact.
The tag is the body of the annotation; lossy — oa:hasBody may also be a textual body, a SpecificResource, etc.
